(Baltimore, Maryland) * [[Montverde Academy]]
([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 13 | draft_team = [[Atlanta Hawks]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[New Orleans Pelicans]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] ({{nbay|2025|end}}) * First-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] ([[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2025]]) * [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]] (2025) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2025) * [[McDonald's All-American Game]] [[Most valuable player|Co-MVP]] ([[2024 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2024]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2024) }} '''Derik Emanuel Queen''' (born December 27, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class. He was drafted 13th overall by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]], but was traded to the Pelicans on draft night. ==High school career== As a freshman, Queen attended [[Saint Frances Academy (Baltimore)|Saint Frances Academy]] in his native [[Baltimore]].{{cite news |last1=Graham |first1=Glenn |last2=Lee |first2=Edward |name-list-style=and |date=February 21, 2024 |title=Derik Queen, a 5-star recruit from Baltimore, commits to Maryland men’s basketball |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2024/02/21/derik-queen-commits-maryland-mens-basketball/ |access-date=February 24, 2024 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]}} On March 12, 2021, he scored a season-high 56 points in a 99–55 win over [[Annapolis Area Christian School]].{{cite news |last=Graham |first=Glenn |date=April 19, 2021 |title=St. Frances basketball star Derik Queen named MaxPreps National Freshman of the Year |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/04/19/st-frances-basketball-star-derik-queen-named-maxpreps-national-freshman-of-the-year/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]}} Queen averaged 14 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two blocks per game during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-shortened]] season, leading the Panthers to a 15–1 record and an appearance in the [[Baltimore Catholic League]] title game. He was named the [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards#Freshman of the Year|MaxPreps National Freshman of the Year]] for his performance. Following the season, Queen transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]].{{cite news |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=July 28, 2021 |title=High school basketball: MaxPreps National Freshman of the Year Derik Queen headed to Montverde Academy, giving Eagles 11 top 60 prospects next season |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/-bRmSUiqyE2IrQ5qTGnDUQ/high-school-basketball-maxpreps-national-freshman-of-the-year-derik-queen-headed-to-montverde-academy%2C-giving-eagles-11-top-60-prospects-next-season.htm |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[MaxPreps]]}} He received limited playing time as a sophomore due to the amount of talent on the team, which won its second straight GEICO Nationals title with a 60–49 win over [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]].{{cite news |last=Schumann |first=Mike |date=January 9, 2023 |title=Rapidly improving 2024 big man Derik Queen gives thoughts on IU basketball, overall recruitment |url=https://www.thedailyhoosier.com/rapidly-improving-2024-big-man-derik-queen-gives-thoughts-on-iu-basketball-overall-recruitment/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=The Daily Hoosier}}{{cite news |last=Hardwig |first=Greg |date=April 2, 2022 |title=High school basketball: Montverde Academy wins sixth GEICO Nationals boys championship |url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/04/02/montverde-academy-wins-sixth-geico-nationals-boys-basketball-championship-fort-myers-link-academy/7199703001/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[The News-Press]]}} On December 9, 2022, Queen recorded his first [[double-double]] at Montverde, contributing 11 points and 11 rebounds during a 78–51 win over [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] at the Bob Kirk Invitational Showcase.{{cite news |title=Derik Queen's Basketball Stats {{!}} Varsity 22-23 |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/fl/montverde/montverde-academy-eagles/athletes/derik-queen/basketball/stats/?careerid=ts8q2t6671sg0&sportSeasonId=77be7c75-cdf9-483d-867f-ea2af557e731#year=22-23 |access-date=February 23, 2024 |publisher=[[MaxPreps]]}}{{cite news |last=Bennett |first=Kyle |date=December 11, 2022 |title=Balanced scoring attack sends Montverde past Oak Hill, 78-51 |url=https://www.times-news.com/sports/local_sports/balanced-scoring-attack-sends-montverde-past-oak-hill-78-51/article_efb2f09e-783e-11ed-afdb-ab9f4200fbbf.html |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[Cumberland Times-News]]}} On December 21, he tallied 13 points and a season-high 16 rebounds in a 79–45 win over [[Milton High School (Georgia)|Milton High School]] at the Iolani Classic.{{cite news |date=December 22, 2022 |title=Boys’ Basketball Closes Out ‘Iolani Classic with Win over Milton |url=https://mvasports.com/news/2022/12/22/boys-basketball-boys-basketball-closes-out-iolani-classic-with-win-over-milton.aspx |access-date=February 23, 2024 |publisher=Montverde Academy Athletics}} On January 5, 2023, Queen scored a season-high 34 points and grabbed 11 rebounds in a 66–62 win over fellow national powerhouse Sunrise Christian Academy at the LaPorte Invitational.{{cite news |last=Branham |first=Travis |date=January 6, 2023 |title=NIBC LaPorte Invitational: Derik Queen, Jayden Ross, Gus Yalden and Matas Buzelis standout on day one |url=https://247sports.com/article/nibc-laporte-invitational-derik-queen-jayden-ross-gus-yalden-and-matas-buzelis-standout-on-day-one-202266616/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[247Sports]]}} The next day, he posted 24 points and 10 rebounds in a 66–61 victory over [[Wasatch Academy]]. On February 3, 2023, Queen recorded 24 points and 13 rebounds to guide second-ranked Montverde to an 85–48 win over top-ranked Link Academy in a highly anticipated matchup between the two top-ranked teams in the country.{{cite news |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=February 3, 2023 |title=High school basketball: National Top 10 No. 2 Montverde Academy blows past previously-unbeaten No. 1 Link Academy 84-58 |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Y5PNgyA7vkCT-QzjCKnIFw/high-school-basketball-national-top-10-no-2-montverde-academy-blows-past-previously-unbeaten-no-1-link-academy-84-58.htm |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[MaxPreps]]}} However, Montverde suffered a 46–45 upset defeat to Sunrise Christian in the quarterfinals of the 2023 GEICO Nationals, which the [[ESPNU]] crew described as "the biggest upset in the 14-year history of the GEICO Nationals."{{cite news |last=Gorches |first=Steve |date=March 30, 2023 |title=Montverde loses to Sunrise in major upset at GEICO High School Nationals |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2023/03/30/montverde-loses-to-sunrise-in-major-upset-at-geico-high-school-nationals/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}} Queen had 10 points and six rebounds in the loss, which ended their season with a record of 23–3. As a junior, he averaged 11.8 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 2.2 assists per game on 61 percent shooting, receiving a [[MaxPreps]] Junior All-American honorable mention.{{cite news |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=June 14, 2023 |title=High school basketball: Derik Queen moves into top 10 of Class of 2024 after dominant spring |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/k6DlOjcE9EWZ8_3AKHmMlA/high-school-basketball-derik-queen-moves-into-top-10-of-class-of-2024-after-dominant-spring.htm |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[MaxPreps]]}} On November 25, 2023, Queen recorded 24 points and eight rebounds to lead Montverde to a 103–74 win over [[Duncanville High School]].{{cite news |title=Derik Queen's Basketball Stats {{!}} Varsity 23-24 |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/fl/montverde/montverde-academy-eagles/athletes/derik-queen/basketball/stats/?careerid=ts8q2t6671sg0&sportSeasonId=66ece839-d183-4227-9807-2e33d599d076#year=23-24 |access-date=February 23, 2024 |publisher=[[MaxPreps]]}} In their next game, an 86–69 victory over [[IMG Academy]], he posted 25 points and 13 rebounds.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |author2-link=Paul Biancardi |name-list-style=and |date=February 21, 2024 |title=Top-10 prospect Derik Queen commits to home state Maryland |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39571528 |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=[[ESPN]]}} On December 8, Queen tallied 20 points and nine rebounds in a 71–59 win over Link Academy. Queen also played for Team Thrill UAA in off-season competitions. In 2023, he led them to an [[Under Armour]] Association (UAA) 17U spring championship after recording 22 points, 15 rebounds and five blocks in their 69–49 title game victory over West Coast Elite.{{cite news|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/k6DlOjcE9EWZ8_3AKHmMlA/high-school-basketball-derik-queen-moves-into-top-10-of-class-of-2024-after-dominant-spring.htm|title=High school basketball: Derik Queen moves into top 10 of Class of 2024 after dominant spring|first=Jordan|last=Divens|work=[[MaxPreps]]|date=June 14, 2023|access-date=February 23, 2024}} ===Recruiting=== Queen was a consensus five-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class, according to major recruiting services. On October 27, 2023, he officially narrowed his list of schools down to four finalists: [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]].{{cite news |last=Tipton |first=Joe |date=October 27, 2023 |title=Top-15 recruit Derik Queen down to 4 schools |url=https://www.on3.com/news/derik-queen-down-to-4-schools-houston-indiana-kansas-maryland/ |access-date=February 23, 2024 |work=On3}} On February 21, 2024, Queen verbally committed to playing [[college basketball]] for Maryland. It was one of the first programs to start recruiting Queen, having offered him a scholarship during the summer before his freshman year. {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2024}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Derik Queen | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Baltimore|Baltimore, MD]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 240 | 40 = | commitdate = February 21, 2024 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | On3 stars = 4 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 93 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2024 | rivals ref title = Maryland 2024 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2024 Maryland Terrapins Recruiting Class | rivals school = maryland | scout s = | espn schoolid = 120 | rivals overall = 18 | 247 overall = 12 | On3 overall = 26 | espn overall = 8 | accessdate = May 30, 2025 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Queen enrolled at the [[University of Maryland]] in 2024. Following his freshman season, he was a first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] selection by the coaches and won the [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]]. In the [[2025 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|2025 Big Ten Tournament]], Queen scored 31 points against the eventual Big Ten champion [[2024–25 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan Wolverines]] in the semifinal. It was the most points ever scored in the tournament by a Maryland freshman and earned him an All-Tournament Team selection.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401743941 |title=Donaldson's court-length drive sends No. 22 Michigan past No. 11 Maryland 81-80 in Big Ten tourney |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 15, 2025 |access-date=March 15, 2025}} In the second round of the subsequent [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Queen scored a fadeaway jump shot at the buzzer to lift Maryland above [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]], 72–71. It was his first game-winning shot at any level.{{cite news |last1=Henderson |first1=Brady |title=Queen's buzzer shot sends Terrapins to Sweet 16 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44378618/derik-queen-buzzer-beater-lifts-maryland-sweet-16 |access-date=March 25, 2025 |work=ESPN.com |date=March 24, 2025 |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===New Orlean Pelicans (2025–present)=== Queen was drafted with the 13th overall pick in the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]], but was traded the same day to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for [[Asa Newell]] and a future first-round draft pick.{{cite web|title=Pelicans acquire draft rights to Derik Queen|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/derik-queen-nba-draft-trade-forward-center-maryland-new-orleans-pelicans-atlanta-hawks-first-round-draft-pick-13|website=NBA.com|date=June 25, 2025|access-date=July 10, 2025}} The pick would turn out to be the 8th pick in the [[2026 NBA Draft]], where the Hawks would draft [[Kingston Flemings]].{{cite web|title=2026 NBA Draft Results: Picks 1-60|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2026-nba-draft-order|website=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2026|access-date=June 23, 2026}} On July 5, 2025, Queen signed his rookie contract.{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans sign rookies Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/jeremiah-fears-derik-queen-new-orleans-pelicans-rookies-signed-roster-update-july-5-2025|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2025|access-date=July 10, 2025}} In a July 15 [[NBA Summer League]] game, Queen tore a [[scapholunate ligament]] in his left wrist. He had surgery on July 18 and was expected to miss three months of action.{{cite news |last1=Leahy |first1=Sean |title= Pelicans rookie Derik Queen out at least 3 months after wrist surgery |url= https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/breaking-news/article/pelicans-rookie-derik-queen-out-at-least-3-months-after-wrist-surgery-210844399.html |access-date=July 20, 2025 |work=[[yahoo.com]] |date=July 18, 2025 }} On November 20, 2025, Queen put up a career-high 30 points, along with nine rebounds, four assists, two steals, and two blocks in a 125–118 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-orleans-pelicans/pelicans-news-new-orleans-may-stink-but-nikola-jokic-sees-vision-derik-queen|title=Pelicans may stink, but Nikola Jokic sees the vision with Derik Queen|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=November 20, 2025|access-date=November 20, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pelicans-derik-queen-logs-career-scoring-high-in-loss/|title=Pelicans' Derik Queen: Logs career scoring high in loss|website=CBS Sports|date=November 20, 2025|access-date=November 20, 2025}} On December 8, Queen put up a triple-double with 33 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists, alongside four blocks in a 135–132 loss to the [[2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]]. He also became the first rookie center to put up a 30-point triple-double in NBA history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-orleans-pelicans/pelicans-news-derik-queen-triple-double-club-luka-lebron-wemby|title=Pelicans’ Derik Queen joins exclusive triple-double club featuring Luka, LeBron, Wemby|website=ClutchPoints|last=Bhatnagar|first=Rishabh|date=December 10, 2025|access-date=December 10, 2025}}{{cite clash|website=espn.com|last=Wright|first=Michael|date=December 9, 2025|access-date=December 9, 2025}} On the final game of the Pelicans' season on April 13, 2026, he put up 30 points and a career-high 22 rebounds in a 132–126 loss to the [[2025–26 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web |last=Eichten |first=Ryan |date=2026-04-13 |title=Timberwolves 132, Pelicans 126: Welcome Home, KG |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/timberwolves-132-pelicans-126-welcome-041738762.html |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=Yahoo Sports }} He finished the season with 11.7 points,
